sentences.text: According to a study by the Fraser Institute cited in a 1999 Alberta health report, overall environmental quality improved by 11% in Canada compared with conditions in 1980, and air pollution decreased significantly during this period.

A 1991 strategic options report noted that the Calvin Lee Report had outlined problems evident in 1986, and by 1991 there were identified weaknesses in environmental health arrangements including lack of direction at an interdepartmental level, lack of a unified voice, and absence of technical resources to deal with new health issues.

Between 1980 and 1991, Alberta's environmental health concerns expanded to include new and complex areas such as how industrial and agricultural development affects human health, in addition to traditional concerns like safe food practices, water and air quality, and safe sewage management.
